title: Adaptive heuristic backoff with idempotency propagation and streaming checkpoint patterns (multi-language SDK)
creator: Ava Chen
description: Define and implement a cross-SDK pattern for adaptive heuristic backoff that propagates idempotency tokens across retries and provides explicit streaming checkpoint tokens for safe resume. Goal: reduce duplicate work and latency spikes, make streaming resume ergonomic across Python/TS/Go SDKs, and ship safe defaults for host applications.
acceptance_criteria: SDKs expose a consistent API for idempotency token propagation (header + SDK-managed body field) across Python/TS/Go

Default backoff uses a hybrid heuristic: small constant retry window for client-visible transient errors, exponential-with-jitter after N attempts, and dynamic safety horizon based on token cost telemetry
Streaming endpoints accept and return a checkpoint token; SDKs can persist and resume streams using that token without duplicating side-effects
Integration tests covering duplicate suppression for common write-like RPCs (create, upsert) and resume tests for chunked streaming uploads
Telemetry emitted for retry_attempt, retry_reason, idemp_token_reused, stream_resume_success, and duplicate_suppressed_count
Feature gated rollout via console flag; rollout doc and migration guide published in docs/sdk/resilience
PRs with language-specific implementations merged and end-to-end example apps updated
technical_notes: Key design constraints: (1) Must be backward-compatible for existing users who do not set idempotency tokens. (2) Minimize surface area change in each SDK idiomatic API. (3) Avoid hard guarantees that require server changes; implement client-side best-effort first with server-assisted optional semantics. Heuristics: start with a 250ms optimistic retry window for HTTP 502/503/504 and transport timeouts for non-idempotent ops if an idempotency token is present; after 2 attempts escalate to exponential backoff with base=200ms, multiplier=2, max=5s and full jitter. Safety horizon: if an operation is potentially expensive (large input size, attachment) the SDK will extend dedup window by reading-cost heuristics. For streaming, the server will return a resume_token on stable checkpoints; SDK will persist the token after each acked checkpoint and attach it to ResumeStream calls. Edge cases: partial side-effect where server returns 202 accepted but no final result; SDK will surface a PendingResult object with poll_with_backoff helper. Performance: add in-process token cache to dedupe duplicate requests originating from app retries. Security: idempotency token is opaque; do not include PII.
api_examples:
from redwood import Client
client = Client()
# idempotent wrapper
with client.operation(idempotency_key='user-123-create-202603') as op:
    op.create_resource(payload)

# streaming resume
stream = client.start_stream(upload_id='file-xyz')
for chunk in read_in_chunks():
    resp = stream.send(chunk)
    if resp.checkpoint:
        save_checkpoint(resp.checkpoint)
# later
checkpoint = load_checkpoint()
stream = client.resume_stream(upload_id='file-xyz', checkpoint=checkpoint)
stream.finish()
telemetry: Emit metric sdk.retry_attempt (tags: sdk_lang, reason, status_code)
Log structured event retry_decision with fields: decision_reason, backoff_ms, attempt_number, idempotency_key_present
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): Ship as opt-in behind SDK feature flag in Python/TS/Go and enable for internal Redwood integration tests. Phase 2 (telemetry validation): enable for 10% of hosted API traffic for new SDK versions; monitor duplicate_suppressed_count and error spike. Phase 3 (gradual default): flip default on for new SDK releases after 2 weeks of stability, provide environment variable to disable behavior. Provide migration guide and changelog entry. Coordinate console feature flag rollout and add an admin toggle for global server-side dedup extension.
migration_notes: For most users: no code changes required unless they want to opt into stronger semantics (pass explicit idempotencyKey). Recommend add idempotencyKey for any non-idempotent REST calls that can be retried by the client. For streaming consumers: call resume with returned checkpoint token. Document how to persist checkpoint and the expected TTL for resume tokens. Backwards compatibility: servers that do not return resume_token will still work; SDK falls back to naive retry without resume when necessary.
